content: ## Purpose of flowcell prep:

label: text
content: ## Flow-cell prep (1): library deposition

label: text
content: - The double-stranded adapter-ligated DNA fragments are denatured with NaOH

label: text
content: - The single stranded DNA molecules are then transferred to the flowcell

label: text
content: - Here, they bind to oligonucleotides ("oligos") attached to the flow cell surface; these oligos are designed to sequences in the adapters

label: text
content: ## Flow-cell prep (1): library deposition

label: text
content: - Extension mix (buffer, dNTP's, Taq polymerase) is pumped into a channel

label: text
content: - The oligos on the flowcell are elongated using the ligated DNA fragments as a templates (reconstruction of the reverse strand of the DNA fragments to be sequenced)

label: text
content: ## Flow-cell prep (1): library deposition

label: text
content: - We now get a double-stranded molecule

label: text
content: ## Flow-cell prep (1): library deposition

label: text
content: - Formamide is added to denature these products, and the original fragment (which is not covalently attached to the flowcell) is washed away

label: text
content: - The reconstructed reverse complement remains covalently fixed to the flowcell!

label: text
content: ## Flow-cell prep (2): bridge amplification

label: text
content: Purpose: amplify single molecules attached to flowcell as described above by factor of 10000000001000 to generate more signal in the following sequencing steps

label: text
content: Single-stranded DNA molecule (1) bends and hybridizes to a second oligo on the flowcell surface (2)

label: text
content: - Extension (reconstruction of reverse complementary strand) is performed all the way back to the other oligo: a "bridge" of double-stranded DNA (3)

label: text
content: - Each strand of the bridge is covalently attached to a different oligo! (3)

label: text
content: - Denaturation seperates the two strands, so that they again can bend and hybridize to another oligo (repeat from step 1, now with twice as many fragments!)

label: text
content: - This is repeated several times to create a cluster of copies of the original DNA fragment!

label: text
content: - Finally: both strands are present; keep only fragments from one of the two strands, those of the reverse strand are cleaved away

label: text
content: ## Sequencing by synthesis

label: text
content: - Sequencing by synthesis (SBS) is relatively simple to understand after all of the prep steps

label: text
content: - Basic idea: reconstruct the reverse strand, but in each "cycle" add only one nucleotide and identify it (A, C, G or T?)

label: text
content: Incorporate one base at a time using four differently marked ddNTPs (fluorescent dyes of different colors)

label: text
content: ★ Difference to Sanger sequence: the ddNTPs have reversible terminators (reversible block of the 3' OH group)

label: text
content: 2 Contemporaneously identify which base was incorporated in each DNA fragment cluster by measuring the wavelength of the incorporated ddNTP

label: text
content: Unblock the ddNTP (remove the terminator such that the sequence can be extended in the next cycle) and repeat!

content: Repeat cycles of sequencing to determine the sequence of bases in a given fragment a single base at a time.

label: text
content: - An imaging step follows each base incorporation step (we speak of one "cycle")

label: text
content: - After each imaging step, the $3^{\prime}$ the $3^{\prime}$ block group is chemically removed and the cycle is repeated.

label: text
content: - After having completed all cycles:

label: text
content: A "base-calling" algorithm assigns sequences and associated quality values ("base qualities") to each "read"

label: text
content: > Read = the sequence of bases called from the colored images for one specific spot of the flow cell, corresponding to one specific DNA fragment!

label: text
content: ## Nanopore sequencing

label: text
content: - A nanopore: A hole of $\sim 1 \mathrm{~}$ nm in diameter

label: text
content: - Apply voltage across pore and observe current due to conduction of ions through the nanopore

label: text
content: - The different bases of DNA block the hole to different extents and change the current in a characteristic way

label: text
content: ## Nanopore sequencing

label: text
content: - By following changes of current over time, we can determine the sequence

label: text
content: - True single-molecule sequencing!

label: text
content: - Advantages: 1) Long reads (>10,00000000000000000 nt); 2) cheap (!)

label: text
content: - Major disadvantage: higher error rates due to signal-to-noise issues inherent in the technology
